$comment: Golden vectors for the shutdown loop status: angular-client computeLoopStatus(withDerivedReadings(readings, now), now) and scylla-server compute_loop_status(apply_derived_readings(...)) must both give these codes (NODE_STATE_CODE, in SHUTDOWN_LOOP order) and verdict. Times are ms.

vectors.name: closed: every reading live and 1, faults clear
unknown: no readings at all
open: single culprit at TSMS
open: unmeasured stretch before the BMS latch
open: EM interlock placeholder and Acc sense suspect
open: a stale HVD reading is no data inside the suspect stretch
open: VCU silent (both frames) blames from the loop start
mismatch: same board, both values held past the grace window
no mismatch: break only 499 ms old
no mismatch: downstream reading flipped back to closed 200 ms ago
no mismatch: cross-board, BMS has not sampled since the break
mismatch: cross-board, a BMS sample after the break still reads closed
CAN latch: every GPIO 0 for 10 s, faults clear: downstream-open, no mismatch
CAN latch: tripped, BSPD 1, GPIOs sampled before the trip: sole suspect, no mismatch
CAN latch: tripped, and a GPIO sampled after the trip still reads closed: mismatch
CAN latch: faults clear, MC HVIL reads 0: both suspect
CAN latch: faults stale, everything else live and 1: closed
CAN latch: a tripped fault that went stale counts as unknown, not tripped
CAN latch: tripped while the BMS latch is already open: downstream-open, reads 0
stale boundary: a 4 Hz reading exactly 3000 ms old is live
stale boundary: a 4 Hz reading 3001 ms old is no data
stale boundary: a single message exactly 60000 ms old is live
stale boundary: a single message 60001 ms old is no data
fresh start: a reading back after going stale gets its own grace window
unmeasured no data: BMS silent, nothing after the EM interlock proves it closed
non-zero values count as closed
